parents.criterion: Enumeration count of evaluation settings and resource markers
parents.instruction: Score 0-10 by counting or estimating how many distinct evaluation settings and resource markers the text enumerates, and nothing else. Count each of: named or counted datasets or benchmarks; named tasks; named languages; named domains; named model architectures or model families; model sizes or parameter counts; transfer, zero-shot, few-shot, or cross-lingual settings named as settings; a stated number of baselines or comparison systems; and explicit scale statements such as compute used, GPU-hours, number of training runs or seeds, number of human annotators, or corpus size. 0 = no evaluation setting or resource marker of any kind is named. 2 = exactly one is named. 5 = roughly three or four distinct settings or counts appear. 8 = five to eight appear, or an explicit large count appears (for example 'twelve benchmarks'). 10 = many appear, or large counts appear across several of these categories at once. This is explicitly NOT a quality judgement. Do not decide whether the coverage is adequate, necessary, convincing, redundant, or excessive; do not consider whether anything was learned in those settings; do not consider whether the comparisons were controlled or fair; do not consider whether the claim is supported. If an item lists many settings and reports no finding at all, it must still be able to score 10. Score only the amount of enumeration present on the page.

parents.criterion: Extent of coverage listing and breadth vocabulary
parents.instruction: Score 0-10 by counting or estimating how much the text lists coverage and how much breadth-signalling vocabulary it uses. Count two things together: (i) the number of listed datasets, benchmarks, tasks, domains, languages, model architectures, model sizes, baselines, or experimental settings, whether named individually or given as a count ('twelve benchmarks', 'six languages'); and (ii) occurrences of breadth-signalling phrasing such as extensive experiments, comprehensive evaluation, a wide range of, across diverse, large-scale, multilingual, cross-domain, cross-lingual, zero-shot, in-the-wild, at scale, or thorough ablations. 0 = the text lists no coverage items and uses no such phrasing. 3 = one or two items or one such phrase. 6 = several listed items, or a coverage phrase plus a short list. 10 = long enumeration across multiple categories, or several breadth phrases stacked together, or both. This is explicitly NOT a quality judgement. Do not decide whether the listed coverage is adequate, appropriate, persuasive, redundant, or padded; do not consider whether the conditions differ in any meaningful way; do not consider whether any result across them is reported; do not consider whether the breadth vocabulary is warranted. An item that lists a dozen benchmarks and reports only 'consistently outperforms' must still be able to score 10.

parents.criterion: Density of formal vocabulary and mathematical notation on the page
parents.instruction: Score 0-10 for the raw extent of formal-mathematical vocabulary and notation in the text, counting or estimating only. Count occurrences of formal-mathematical vocabulary such as theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, proof, bound, convergence, rate, assumption, regularity, convexity, smoothness, optimality, minimax, complexity, estimator, guarantee, and close relatives; and any inline notation such as Greek letters, single-letter variable names, subscripts or superscripts, norms, expectations, probability symbols, big-O or Omega expressions, inequalities, set or operator symbols, or displayed formulas. 0 = none of these markers appears anywhere. 3 = one or two isolated markers in the whole text. 7 = markers recur across several sentences. 10 = such vocabulary and notation are dense from the first sentence to the last. This is explicitly NOT a quality judgement. Do not consider whether the formalism is correct, rigorous, necessary, well used, or informative; do not consider whether anything is actually proved; do not consider whether symbols are defined or whether assumptions are stated; do not consider whether the prose is clear. An item saturated with symbols that states nothing a reader could check must still be able to score 10.
